source_book: NCERT Class 11 Ch.5 Laws of Motion — table-of-contents reference only (Newton's first law / inertia is a standalone lead section, before Newton's second law); teaching authored from first principles. The atomic idea: a body's velocity stays exactly constant (including v = 0) unless a NET external force acts on it. Does NOT cover how much a net force changes velocity (newton_second_law), force pairs (newton_third_law), drawing all forces on a body (free_body_diagram), or the friction-threshold model (block_on_incline / friction_static_kinetic). Engine: the shared newtons_laws_body field_3d scenario (docs/NEWTONS_LAWS_BODY_ENGINE_SPEC.md) — a flat surface (theta_deg = 0) carrying one body, gravity resolved into weight/normal, optional friction, no applied force, no pulley. All four states are expressible with the engine's existing config surface; ENGINE GAP: none.

real_world_anchor.primary: A space probe coasting between planets — its engines shut off years ago, and it has not slowed by a single meter per second, because nothing out there pushes it or drags it, so it keeps its velocity forever.
real_world_anchor.secondary: Slide the same object across a rough table and it dies within half a meter; slide it across smooth ice and it glides much farther — the closer the surface gets to frictionless, the closer real life gets to the space probe.

aha_moment.statement: Nothing keeps something moving at constant velocity — only a net force changes it.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: The block glides the full length of the frictionless floor at an unchanging v while the net-force readout holds 0.00 the entire time; on the identical launch with friction switched on (STATE_2), a visible backward arrow appears and the block stops.

constraints: g = 9.8 m/s^2 (Earth's surface, constant, theta = 0 throughout this concept)
ideal rigid body, no deformation, no air resistance or drag anywhere in this concept
under kinetic friction with theta = 0, deceleration a = -mu_k * g is mass-independent (m cancels)
static-hold condition abs(drive) <= mu_s * N is never near its threshold in any authored state
STOP_EPS_V = 0.01 m/s: velocity below this is treated as exactly zero by the engine
mass and weight are not the same physical quantity (w = m*g, not m itself)

STATE_1.title: Frictionless coast: constant v, zero net force

scene_composition.text: Frictionless floor: block set moving once, keeps going forever
v holds constant, F_net = 0.00 the whole time
like a space probe coasting between planets — nothing pushes it, nothing drags it

tts_sentences.text_en: Watch the number v — it never changes.
This block was set moving once, and now glides forever on a frictionless floor, exactly like a space probe coasting between planets.
Net force reads zero the whole time: nothing pushes it, nothing drags it, so nothing changes its velocity.

STATE_2.title: Contrast: same launch, friction on — a real force stops it

scene_composition.text: Same launch, same v0 — friction switched on this time
arrow f k glows from frame 1, pointing backward
block stops in ~4 s: a real named force, not motion wearing off

tts_sentences.text_en: Same launch, same starting speed — but now a real backward force, friction, pushes from the surface.
Watch the arrow f k glow from the very first frame.
The block visibly slows and stops in about four seconds, not because motion wears off, but because this named force stops it.

misconception_watch.belief: Moving things stop on their own; keeping something moving needs a continuous push (the Aristotelian default — every object the student has ever pushed eventually stopped).
misconception_watch.visual_counter: Two identical launches, same v0 — the ONLY change is friction. Frictionless, F_net stays 0.00 and the block never slows (STATE_1); with friction, a named, visible backward arrow does the stopping, and the block dies within a couple of meters.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Things don't stop on their own — a real backward force stops them.

STATE_3.title: Rest is balanced forces: N = mg, F_net = 0

scene_composition.text: weight mg down, normal N up — full-size arrows, both real
drag m: both arrows rescale together, block never moves, F_net stays 0.00

tts_sentences.text_en: This block sits still, yet two forces act on it: weight m g pulling down, and normal force N pushing up exactly as hard.
They balance exactly — net force sigma F stays zero — so the block never moves.
Rest means balanced forces, never absent ones.

misconception_watch.belief: An object at rest has no forces acting on it.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: Two full-length arrows sit on the resting block — mg down, N up — while the net-force readout is pinned at 0.00: big forces, zero net, zero motion.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Rest is balanced forces, not absent forces.

STATE_4.title: Explore: drive m, F, mu_s, mu_k, v0 — when does v change?

scene_composition.text: Set mass, force, mu_s, mu_k, v0 — watch v, a, f, F_net, N
F = 0 and friction = 0 -> v stays exactly constant

tts_sentences.text_en: Your turn — set mass, force, and the friction coefficients, and watch velocity, acceleration, and net force respond live.
